verdicts.reason: No substantive analysis; does not identify the Sacklers as beneficiaries.
No discussion distinguishing direct creditor claims from estate claims.
No discussion of nonconsenting claimants or compelled extinguishment.
No recognition that the Sacklers did not enter bankruptcy.
No explanation of the contribution-for-protection exchange.
No discussion of creditor voting versus universal consent.
No discussion of district court rejection or Second Circuit approval.
No use or characterization of the respondent brief.
No discussion of section 105(a).
No discussion of section 1123(b)(6).
No explanation of the catchall’s contextual reading.
No distinction between estate-owned claims and direct claims.
No explanation that the release functions as a nondebtor discharge.
No discussion of discharge limits and burdens.
No explanation that contribution size does not supply statutory authority.
No discussion of section 524(g) or the asbestos exception.
No statement that the Supreme Court reversed and remanded.
No statement preserving consensual third-party releases.
No statement that the Court left the consent standard open.
No discussion of full satisfaction of third-party claims.
No discussion of substantially consummated plans.
No distinction between release authority and merits of opioid claims.
No explanation that remand leaves further negotiations unresolved.
No limited statement of the operative holding.
No discussion of the dissent’s collective-recovery argument.
No labeling or discussion of the dissent.
No discussion of funding or recovery risks.
No consideration of a consensual revision.
No discussion of preserving estate-claim settlements while separating direct claims.
No request to identify claim owners and release beneficiaries.
No request for consent mechanism or affected population.
No discussion of confirming continued funding or revised conditions on remand.
